scored_by: Worked example — Meridian Care Logistics is fictional. Nothing here is a real vendor.
summary: A scheduling-and-routing optimizer built for multi-site home health, with a live bi-directional HCHB integration and a strong week-level engine. Capacity is modelled as visit points against a productivity target, which matches how Compassus already reasons. Patient engagement is thin — reminders and confirmations exist, agentic outreach does not — and the clinician-facing model is advisory by design.

hchb.note: Live since Mar 2024, four HCHB customers, published API both directions. Conflict resolution described: HCHB is authoritative for orders, Meridian for assignment.

CAP-01.quote: roster synced nightly by discipline, role and FTE

CAP-02.quote: assessing vs non-assessing is a role flag, not its own capacity pool

CAP-04.quote: per-diem pool modelled as elastic supply

CAP-06.quote: PTO from HCHB, working patterns maintained in product

CAP-07.quote: zip-level territory with branch coverage overlay

CAP-08.quote: drive-time isochrones from home base, refreshed quarterly

CAP-09.quote: visit points per type against a per-clinician weekly target

CAP-10.quote: committed vs open by day, discipline and territory

CAP-11.quote: referral inflow modelled; discharge outflow not forecast

SCH-01.quote: orders and frequencies read from HCHB

SCH-02.quote: auth status attached per visit, payer rules configurable

SCH-03.quote: held state — ordered but not schedulable, with a reason code

SCH-04.quote: compliance window enforced as a hard constraint

SCH-05.quote: discipline, competency and acuity weighted in the match

SCH-07.quote: patient availability captured, but by office staff not the platform

SCH-08.quote: cadence supported; infection-control sequencing not addressed

SCH-10.quote: route proximity and mileage optimised per day

SCH-12.quote: front-loading and week balancing against plan-of-care pace

SCH-13.quote: missed visits tracked with cause coding

SCH-14.quote: reassignment inside the compliance window, offered by rank

ENG-02.quote: staff see and control all outreach — but all of it is staff-initiated

ENG-04.quote: captured in product, entered by a coordinator

ENG-05.quote: SMS reminders and en-route ping from the clinician app

ENG-06.quote: confirmation round exists, run by staff from a worklist

ENG-09.quote: reschedule is a staff task with a suggested slot

ENG-10.quote: open need broadcast to eligible clinicians in the app

ENG-11.quote: call-out triggers a ranked coverage offer within minutes

ENG-13.quote: no-show logged and requeued; follow-up is manual

ENG-14.quote: multi-discipline coordination on the shared week view

ENG-16.quote: clinician sees own schedule, points and mileage

S1.note: Optimiser decides against the envelope and shows a branch leader the impact of accepting a referral before they accept it.

S2.note: Engine assigns across competency, capacity, continuity and drive time together.

S3.note: Plans and rebalances the week against plan-of-care pace; a scheduler confirms.

S4.note: Held state with reason codes, auto-releases on auth, then proposes a slot.

S5.note: Call-out triggers a ranked offer automatically, escalates to per-diem, then to the DCS worklist.

D1.note: Clinician can decline and reorder their own day; cannot change assignment. Declines feed a preference weight.

D2.note: Designed to advise; decide mode is a per-branch configuration with a documented migration path.

D3.note: Adoption defined as weekly active use. No six-month curve supplied.

P1.note: Open to design-partner pricing and a joint roadmap. No structure or terms proposed.

P2.note: Three named deployments, a resistance story, and a change they made because of it — moved from decide to advise.

P3.note: Raised payer-mix-aware sequencing, which is not on our one-pager.

P4.note: Chose not to build patient-facing voice; says the EMR should own the record of contact.

differentiators: Only answer that gives a branch leader the envelope impact of accepting a referral **before** they accept it (C1).
Coverage offer with a measured median time-to-fill — 4 minutes — rather than a described workflow (C5).
Decide-vs-advise is a per-branch switch with a migration path, not a product-wide posture (D2).
Raised payer-mix-aware sequencing, which is not on our one-pager and probably should be (E1).

flags.text: Measured impact (A3) comes from one site. References offered but not yet named.
All patient outreach is staff-initiated — the coordinator labour we are trying to remove stays.
Hospice and private duty are 40% of their business; home health is not the whole company.

unknowns: On-call and weekend rotation load (CAP-05) — not addressed anywhere in the return.
Whether discharge outflow can be forecast, or only observed (CAP-11).
What the day-before confirmation round actually costs in staff hours at our scale.
E2 — what a value-share would concretely look like. Needs a direct conversation.
